name: Cameralism
summary: Cameralism was the 18th-century German science of managing the territorial state: a bureaucracy trained in finance, economy and Polizei raises revenue, population and productive output for the monarch while promoting subjects' welfare. It favours state-directed economic life, import substitution and a favourable trade balance, and puts trained officials in charge under a strong monarch.
scope: The German and Austrian cameralist tradition from Seckendorff (Teutscher Fürstenstaat, 1656) through Justi, Sonnenfels and Jung-Stilling's 1788 textbook; excludes neocameralism and later welfare-state or Prussian-socialist readings. Modern topics are mostly answered by inference at low confidence.

keyFigures.name: Veit Ludwig von Seckendorff
keyFigures.role: Early theorist often regarded as founder of cameralism, author of Teutscher Fürstenstaat.

keyFigures.name: Johann Heinrich Gottlob von Justi
keyFigures.role: Leading cameralist professor and systematiser of Polizei and finance.

keyFigures.name: Joseph von Sonnenfels
keyFigures.role: Viennese cameralist who taught and advised the Habsburg administration.

sources.title: Johann Heinrich Gottlob Justi (Wikipedia)
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Justi's modern commercial monarchies, respect for private property, tax reform, reduced guild power.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Cameralist Polizei included public health, physicians and medical regulation as state duties, but a modern tax-funded universal system is anachronistic; inferred from the state's duty to promote subjects' welfare and population.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Cameralists regulated wages and prices in the guild and Polizei order, but a minimum wage as a worker-protective policy was never discussed; they would favour whatever raised productive population, so the answer is split.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Cameralism assumed officials must steer economic life and that individuals cannot be trusted to serve the common good unaided, though later cameralists like Justi wanted fewer monopolies and guild restrictions.

public-ownership.rationale: Cameralist princes ran crown estates, mines, forests and manufactories as the core revenue base, so state ownership of productive enterprise was standard; modern utilities are an extension, hence not the strongest.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Justi and Sonnenfels wrote tax rules aimed at state revenue and fairness to the productive classes, not at redistribution; progressive taxation of the rich was not a stated goal and adherents would be split.

unions-good.rationale: Cameralists organized labour through state-supervised guilds and Polizei regulation, and Justi wanted to curb guild power; autonomous workers' associations would compete with the sovereign's administration.

property-fundamental.rationale: Justi held that a successful state requires moderate government respecting private property, yet cameralists also let the sovereign direct land use and economy for state ends, so property is secure but not near-absolute.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Cameralist Polizei regulated manufactures, trade companies and commerce in detail to serve state welfare, so tighter regulation of enterprise fits, though Justi also backed chartered trade companies.

cut-welfare.rationale: Cameralists made care for the poor and the productive employment of subjects a state duty, though with work compulsion for idlers; cutting welfare for dependency reasons is not their line.

worker-ownership.rationale: Cameralism was a top-down administrative doctrine in which the sovereign and his officials organize production; collective ownership by workers has no place in its sources.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Cameralist Polizei relied on census, registers and close information gathering about every subject, and Jung-Stilling treats policing of dangerous sects as normal state practice.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not addressed directly; cameralist Polizei policed morals, vice and subjects' habits paternalistically, so adult free choice on drugs is inferred as disfavoured.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed; cameralist Polizei censored books and speech harming the state or religion, which suggests restriction, but toward hatred of groups specifically there is no source, so left split.

strong-leader.rationale: The cameralist model is a strong monarch acting through an efficient bureaucracy to reform the country without estates blocking him; Justi judged only a modernised monarchy able to carry out sweeping reform.

state-harmful.rationale: Cameralism exists to strengthen the state and its administration, and treats the state as the instrument of public happiness.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed; Polizei regulation of arms for public safety and a state monopoly on organised force fit cameralist administration, but the evidence is inferential.

empower-police-military.rationale: Seckendorff and Justi made security and a strong army essential to the state's power, and Polizei was the era's main domestic administrative arm.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: A cameralist writer in Small's survey would tolerate regulated brothels for reasons of state while moral writers condemned them, so adherents split.

decide-locally.rationale: Cameralism arose to centralise and standardise administration in each territory under the prince's collegial bodies, against estates and local privileges.

rehabilitation.rationale: Cameralists favoured workhouses to make idlers productive and discussed penal reform, but also harsh policing; Justi-era writers differed on punishment.

traditional-family.rationale: Cameralist writers treated the household and marriage as the base of Oeconomie and promoted marriage and large families to raise population.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not discussed; the 18th-century Polizei state regulated marriage to promote population and morals, so inferred opposition.

abortion-legal.rationale: Population growth was a core cameralist aim, and Polizei strictly punished concealed births and infanticide, so legal abortion is inferred as opposed.

more-religion-public.rationale: Cameralists considered religion a state concern and ruler duty, but Justi and Jung-Stilling stressed toleration and keeping religion useful to civil welfare; adherents ranged from pietist to enlightened.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: The question is anachronistic to cameralism; no source addresses it, and a state-led correction is neither stated nor excluded.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Anachronistic; cameralist texts do not address the nature of gender and nothing supports a position either way.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Cameralists served territorial states rather than a national culture and imported foreign talent freely, though Seckendorff wrote in German for the German fatherland; no clear position.

gradual-change.rationale: Cameralists were reforming officials who wanted sweeping administrative change by royal decree, yet also worked through existing institutions and warned against abrupt changes. No cited source addresses this statement directly.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Cameralists wanted population growth and actively encouraged skilled immigration and settlement as a source of state wealth.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Cameralists focused on the territorial sovereign's power in a competitive state system; Justi wrote about the balance of Europe, not supranational bodies, so inferred disagreement.

free-trade.rationale: Cameralism resembled mercantilism with import substitution and protection of domestic manufactures; Justi sought removal of some domestic bans but a favourable foreign balance.

nation-first.rationale: Cameralism put the sovereign state's strength and wealth ahead of others in a competitive system, though the modern notion of 'nation' is anachronistic.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Not addressed; war served the interests of the sovereign state in this era, so an intervention for human rights is inferred as foreign.

open-borders.rationale: Cameralist states controlled movement and keeping subjects within the territory was part of population policy, even as they welcomed selected immigrants.

limit-growth.rationale: Increasing production, population and national wealth was the central aim of cameralism. No cited source addresses this statement directly.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic; the cameralists did care for forestry and resource management, but nothing supports a position on climate.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Cameralist training covered natural sciences, mining and husbandry, and officials expected improved technique and manufactures to increase wealth.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Anachronistic; cameralists would back whatever state-directed energy policy raises output, but nothing was stated.

revolution-justified.rationale: Cameralism is the administrative doctrine of the absolute monarch and treats subjects' duty of obedience as basic; Justi sought reform from above.

experts-over-public.rationale: Cameralism trained a professional civil service in a science of administration to run the state, and distrusted individuals' capacity to know what serves the public welfare.

central-planning.rationale: Cameralists wanted comprehensive state management of production but within a private-and-crown economy of household production, not a planned economy in the modern sense; adherents split on reading.

socialized-markets.rationale: The question assumes worker or public ownership with markets; cameralists accepted markets under state direction but not worker ownership, so a mild disagree.

land-value-tax.rationale: Cameralist fiscal policy used crown domains, regalia and a range of taxes, and Justi wrote on balanced tax systems rather than a single tax on land.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Not addressed by the cameralists in the sources opened; inheritance taxes were not in their programs.

basic-income.rationale: Cameralist welfare meant organised care for the poor tied to compulsory work in workhouses; unconditional payment contradicts their view that idlers be put to work.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Import substitution, protection of domestic manufactures and a favourable balance of trade were central cameralist instruments.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Cameralists had the prince establish manufactures, mines and trading companies, giving credit and privileges to strategic industries.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Cameralist writers valued a prosperous peasantry and artisans but also crown domains and large estates; the question is not a defining concern.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Cameralism aimed at accumulating money and wealth in the state; abolishing money would contradict its fiscal science (Kameral).

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Cameralists managed money, coinage and credit as state business, so leaving money to the market contradicts their approach.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Cameralist states supervised guilds that set prices and wages, but tripartite bargaining bodies as modern corporatism did not exist; adherents like Justi also wanted guild power reduced.

one-party-rule.rationale: No parties existed; cameralism assumed monarchical rule through a collegial bureaucracy, not a single ideological party, so mild disagreement.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Cameralism is the science of managing the monarchical state, and Justi held a modernised monarchy was the only form able to carry through economic reform.

democracy-best.rationale: Cameralists favoured absolutist or paternalist monarchy for the welfare of subjects; Justi concluded monarchy was best for reform, though he opposed despotism.

direct-votes.rationale: Cameralism rests on administration by trained officials under the sovereign; popular votes on laws find no place.

workers-councils.rationale: Political power rested in the monarch and his colleges of officials; workers' councils are foreign to cameralism. No cited source addresses this statement directly.

right-to-secede.rationale: Cameralism built larger more efficient territorial states and Justi wanted bigger German states to rival France and England, so secession cuts against it.

natural-rulers.rationale: Cameralists assumed rule by the prince and his educated officials, and the gentry were to be educated in estate management; birth and training qualified rulers.

political-violence-never.rationale: Cameralist authors treated state force as legitimate for security and war while rejecting rebellion, so the statement's blanket form splits them.

war-builds-character.rationale: Cameralists valued military power as a function of the state's wealth, but Justi wrote against the European balance as a source of wars; character-building is not their argument.

separate-church-state.rationale: Cameralist national management included religion and morals, and the prince supervised the church, though Justi and Jung-Stilling favoured toleration of non-harmful faiths.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Cameralism rested on natural law and the sovereign's reason with Christian principles as a moral guide for Polizei, not on scriptural law as such; Seckendorff was more religious than Justi.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Courts, policing and defence were core sovereign functions in the cameralist state. No cited source addresses this statement directly.

military-superiority.rationale: Cameralists aimed to raise state revenue and power to rival other states in military strength.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Territorial states in the Empire were multi-ethnic dynastic states, and cameralists welcomed immigrants of any origin who added to the population.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Cameralism held that the interests of ruler and people align and that estates should be harmonised under the sovereign. No cited source addresses this statement directly.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Cameralist society was ordered by estates with differentiated duties; the aim was general happiness and prosperity, not equality.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Anachronistic and not addressed by cameralist writers, who dealt with territorial states in Germany.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Anachronistic; cameralism contrasted itself with colonial mercantilism and said nothing on reparations.

civilizational-union.rationale: Cameralists worked within separate German territorial states and did not propose unions by civilization; Justi wanted larger states, but within the Empire.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Cameralists held that individuals cannot be trusted and that officials guide subjects toward the common good, though Justi saw ruler and subjects' happiness as linked.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Cameralist and Pietist texts stress duties of subjects and rulers, though Jung-Stilling speaks of 'rights of humanity' that the state protects as well.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Cameralists treated nature as a resource for state revenue, forestry and farming; intrinsic value is a modern idea.

limit-population.rationale: Population increase was a central cameralist goal, as the source of labour, soldiers and tax revenue.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Cameralists sought to spread manufactures and raise output, regarding them as sources of national wealth.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Cameralists promoted manufactures and applied science but within an ordered administrative framework, so an agree without 'disrupting institutions' emphasis.

human-enhancement.rationale: Anachronistic; no cameralist source speaks to bodily enhancement and the paternalist state could go either way.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anachronistic; cameralists' preference for rational expert administration and statistics hints at openness, but nothing was stated.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Cameralist Polizei sought full information on subjects and censored, so a state-unreadable communication is inferred as opposed.

restore-past-order.rationale: Cameralists were reformers building a more efficient modern state against the older estate-based order; they wanted progress in administration and prosperity.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Cameralism was a practical administrative science judged by revenue, population and welfare outcomes rather than by doctrine.

direct-action.rationale: Change was to come from the sovereign and his officials; subjects acting on their own was disorder. No cited source addresses this statement directly.

means-match-ends.rationale: Cameralist authors did not discuss this principle, and nothing in the sources supports a side.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Cameralism was about raising productivity through agriculture, mining, and manufactures. No cited source addresses this statement directly.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Cameralists encouraged manufactures, trades and specialised industries as means to wealth.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Cameralists wanted help for the needy but set work as a duty ('he who does not work is not worthy to eat'), with property distributed through existing orders.

production-for-use.rationale: Cameralists sought production for state and subject welfare yet relied on markets, money and profit by artisans and merchants; split.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The exploitation theory is a later socialist doctrine; cameralists saw trade and manufacture profits as sources of national wealth.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Foreign to a doctrine of monarchical administration with estates under the prince. No cited source addresses this statement directly.

collective-farming.rationale: Cameralists wanted to improve private peasant and domain agriculture through state encouragement, not collectivise it.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Anachronistic; cameralists saw war as a normal state function and wealth as its basis, not a result of capitalism.

taxation-theft.rationale: Revenue extraction was the core of Kameral science, and Justi wrote guidelines for taxation to strengthen the state.

harm-principle.rationale: Cameralist Polizei regulated morals and conduct for the subjects' happiness; Jung-Stilling allows liberty only so far as it harms no one but also expects the state to promote perfection.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Jung-Stilling speaks of rights of humanity (person, property, honour, liberty) for individuals while cameralists emphasised duties and estates; unresolved.

conscription.rationale: Seckendorff-era writers argued for universal military duty, as shown in Small's survey, and cameralist states drew soldiers from the population.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Cameralists sought to retain and enlarge the population and regarded emigration as a loss. No cited source addresses this statement directly.

state-as-business.rationale: The cameralist prince ran the territory like a large estate, but subjects' happiness, not customers' choice, was the aim, so neither side fits cleanly.

positive-liberty.rationale: Justi stated the state must guarantee freedom and promote the happiness of free beings, which implies provision of means, but modern 'positive liberty' wording is anachronistic.

media-academia-power.rationale: Not addressed; cameralist theorists were themselves professors who wanted universities to train officials, so they would not see them as a rival to government.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Anachronistic; cameralist texts do not discuss race and no position can be documented.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Cameralists considered administrative science to be rational and teachable knowledge to improve the state; the postmodern claim is foreign.

universal-morality.rationale: Justi tied cameralism to natural law, and Jung-Stilling derives the state's purpose from natural rights knowable to reason and Christian morals.

single-common-good.rationale: Cameralism assumes a single common welfare and happiness that the ruler and educated officials determine, not a balancing of interests.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Anachronistic, with no cameralist source on it.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Anachronistic, with no cameralist source on it.

revive-national-language.rationale: Not addressed; Seckendorff argued for writing in German rather than Latin, but reviving a lost language is a different matter.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Administration was hierarchical in the cameralist state; workers' or public votes in running enterprises are foreign to it.

school-vouchers.rationale: Cameralists wanted state-organised education for officials and subjects; choice financed by vouchers is inferred as against that.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Cameralism was fundamentally about sound public finance and accumulating revenue, so large deficits were to be avoided, though Keynesian stimulus is anachronistic.

economic-freedom.rationale: Cameralists did not make political liberty depend on economic liberty; their model joined state direction of the economy with an obedient monarchy.

rule-by-example.rationale: Seckendorff's Christian princely mirror stressed the ruler's own virtue but Polizei and law were the main means, so the answer is split.

national-self-determination.rationale: Cameralist loyalty was to the dynastic territorial state; self-determination of nations is a later idea.

force-without-un.rationale: Anachronistic, since the UN did not exist, but cameralists accepted sovereign war-making without external approval, so an agreement is inferred but weakly.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Justi's cameralism followed natural law and Enlightenment rationalism, while Seckendorff and Jung-Stilling gave Christian faith a central role; adherents are split.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: No documented position; cameralists cared for the poor in the territory and wanted to attract immigrants as subjects.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Cameralists made vagrants and idlers work and held that those who do not work should not eat; workhouses were typical.

class-collaboration.rationale: Cameralists held ruler, estates and subjects to share an interest in general happiness and wanted guild and trade groups subordinated to common welfare.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Cameralists founded libraries, universities and academies to train officials and for national management; destroying heritage was no goal.

dominated-front.rationale: Anachronistic and not a cameralist concern.

workers-nation.rationale: Anachronistic; cameralism has no concept of a working-class international or nation.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Not addressed directly; the household economy of the period gave men and women distinct roles and cameralist writers assumed that order.

ban-interest.rationale: Cameralists ran credit institutions such as banks and montes pietatis and treated money circulation as a state interest, not interest bans.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Cameralists valued population growth and welcomed settlers and no cameralist source classifies subjects by race.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Cameralism presents the state as serving the common happiness of all subjects, not any one class.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Anachronistic; cameralists did encourage mining and domestic resource extraction, which points toward domestic production but weakly.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Cameralists wanted immigrants settled and productive, and the sources do not say whether they expected cultural assimilation.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy theory with no place in cameralist sources, which welcomed population growth by immigration. No cited source addresses this statement directly.

proportional-representation.rationale: Cameralism assumed no elected legislature at all; the principle of proportional party representation is foreign, so a mild disagree.

national-mission.rationale: Cameralist aims were internal prosperity and territorial strength, not spreading a form of government abroad.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Anachronistic; the cameralist household order assumed male headship as natural.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Cameralists staked their programme on the competence and honesty of trained officials, and Justi proposed colleges to keep the ruler virtuous.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: No cameralist source supports it; their population policy was pro-natalist, although regulation of marriage was normal.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Not addressed; the sovereign was answerable to God and law in Seckendorff's view, not to a modern accountability for security forces.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Cameralists made the state manage the economy, morals, education and welfare, far beyond defence and justice.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: No cameralist source supports it and population growth was prized.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Jung-Stilling affirms natural rights for all and Seckendorff said salvation is equal for peasant and king, while civil status stayed unequal by estate. No cited source addresses this statement directly.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Anachronistic; cameralism contrasts with colonial mercantilism and says nothing on settler states.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Cameralists sought uniform administration and standardised law within the territorial state, though religious personal law question was not discussed.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Jung-Stilling allows religious parties to continue as long as they cause no harm, while others of the period restricted sects; split.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Cameralists encouraged livestock husbandry and meat and hide production as agricultural wealth; the idea of a ban is foreign.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Christian education of subjects was a Polizei duty in the cameralist state.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A socialist state is outside this ideology, but the state's strength against rivals is a general cameralist premise; no direct view.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Justi's idea was that people entrusted collective pursuit of happiness to one ruler, a contract-like origin; legitimacy rests on serving welfare rather than present consent.

trade-surplus.rationale: A favourable balance of foreign trade was one of Justi's three sources of national wealth and cameralism is mercantilist in this.

population-transfer.rationale: No source supports expelling minorities; cameralists wanted more subjects, although religious dissenters were sometimes banished in the era.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Cameralism emphasised administrative order and cooperation under the ruler, though states competed for power.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Jung-Stilling permits suppression of sects whose teachings harm the state, which extends to groups seeking to overturn the order.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Cameralism accepted the monarch's discretionary power, restrained by moral virtue and administrative colleges rather than law-based non-domination.

separated-powers.rationale: Justi was influenced by Montesquieu and proposed colleges, but cameralists kept the prince as sole source of power; split.

vanguard-party.rationale: Foreign to cameralism, which relies on the prince's bureaucracy. No cited source addresses this statement directly.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Care for the poor was a state task, but the aim was common happiness and productive employment, not priority to any group.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Anachronistic; the cameralist state owned domain property and was not oriented to selling it to tenants.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Cameralist Polizei suppressed disorder in trades and journeymen combinations were policed, so restriction is inferred, with a secret ballot requirement being modern.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Cameralists held that a larger population is the source of wealth and power, not of poverty.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Cameralists welcomed settlers and skilled immigrants of various religions and origins, so diversity was not seen as a threat.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Cameralist offices were filled by educated officials appointed by the ruler, trained by cameralist courses.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The sovereign had full discretion in states of necessity in the absolutist state, though Jung-Stilling stresses rights, so a modest agree.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Polizei regulated grain, bread and meat prices and provisioning, and magazines against scarcity were standard cameralist practice, though Justi favoured freer grain export in good times.

party-controls-media.rationale: No party existed, but cameralists backed book censorship and state control of printing; Jung-Stilling wanted police limits on harmful publications.

party-commands-army.rationale: No parties; the prince commanded the army through his officials.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Cameralist states sought to attract settlers and speedy subject status to raise population.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: No legislature of elected representatives exists in the model; officials were salaried by rank.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Parties are outside cameralism, and nothing supports a side.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Cameralists strengthened the sovereignty of territorial princes, so pooling sovereignty in a supranational union is inferred as unwelcome, though they lived within the Empire.

head-commands-forces.rationale: In the cameralist monarchy the sovereign commanded the army and chose his ministers and college officials.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Cameralists across Lutheran, Reformed and Catholic territories differed, and Justi converted to Catholicism; no common position.

clerical-rule.rationale: The prince and his civil administration ruled, with religion supervised as one branch of Polizei; clerics had no highest authority.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Subjects owe obedience to the sovereign, who directs the war effort. No cited source addresses this statement directly.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Cameralist Polizei supervised book censorship and public morals, and Jung-Stilling wants police to prevent harmful publications and theatre.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Presidents do not exist in the cameralist model; the monarch ruled for life, so the question does not separate adherents.

recall-officials.rationale: Officials answered to the sovereign and his colleges, not to voters, so recall by voters is foreign.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Cameralist states sought military strength and Justi criticised a balance-of-power doctrine, but alliances were normal tools of princely policy.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: The state ordering of towns, markets and property did not abolish tenancies; cameralist urban policy supervised rents and lodging.

people-in-arms.rationale: Cameralist writers proposed universal duty for military service but organised armies under state discipline, so a citizens' militia replacing the army is a mild disagree.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Agriculture was the base of state wealth for the cameralists, who valued peasants, but they also promoted towns and manufactures.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Anachronistic; cameralists served particular German territorial states, though Justi wanted larger states.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Cameralism put university-trained officials at the heart of government and founded professorships to train them. No cited source addresses this statement directly.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Anachronistic; Justi admired China's bureaucracy but cameralist works contain no relativist doctrine.

death-penalty.rationale: Cameralist-era writers differed on executions; Jung-Stilling treats it as an open question, and Sonnenfels argued against it as against the aims of the state. No cited source addresses this statement directly.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Anachronistic; Polizei-era morals regulation implies a cautious approach, but cameralists did not address such curricula.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Not addressed; Christian education was supported but natural sciences were part of cameralist training.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Polizei suppressed indecent publications and prostitution outside regulation as part of state control of morals.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Territorial states recruited immigrants and subject status followed residence and allegiance; no source requires descent.

minority-language-support.rationale: Not addressed; Seckendorff defended writing in German rather than Latin, but support to minority languages was not a concern.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Jung-Stilling tolerates harmless sects but limits any teaching or practice that damages civil society, and the state sets common law.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Cameralist Polizei sought to shape subjects' morals and habits and assumed that people could not be trusted to rule themselves.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Cameralists prized sound public credit and debt repayment, and the question is anachronistic in the colonial sense.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Constitutions were not drafted by assemblies; the monarch and his administration fixed the order. No cited source addresses this statement directly.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Cameralism assumes that the sovereign may direct subjects and curb liberties to build the state's wealth and strength.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Anachronistic; cameralists addressed care of the state's own poor and subjects.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Anachronistic; the sovereign's own military capability was valued, but nothing was stated.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The head of state was a hereditary monarch in the cameralist state. No cited source addresses this statement directly.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Currency and finance were state business of the ruler's treasury (Kameral), not placed in an independent body.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Not addressed; the territorial prince's land was his state's basis but dynastic bargaining was normal.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Cameralist doctrine subordinated individual economic action to common welfare, even as Justi respected private property.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Anachronistic and outside cameralism; no position.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Cameralists regulated forestry and resources for the long-run state interest, but the principle is anachronistic.

collective-defense.rationale: Alliances were tools of princely policy and Justi doubted the European balance; no clear position.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Dynastic states acquired territory by conquest and treaty, without any test of consent of the people.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Cameralist national management included religion, and the prince supervised church affairs; Justi clashed with ecclesiastical authorities.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The monarch ruled actively in cameralism rather than standing above politics as a symbol, but he did stand above parties, so no clear answer.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Cameralists built and consolidated strong territorial states, and the prince would defend its integrity by force.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Cameralism aimed at standardising law and the economy in a state, so a region keeping a separate system runs against it.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Seckendorff's ruler is an office holder with duties before God, and Justi's ruler serves subjects' welfare, neither sacred nor divine in descent.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Income tax was not in the cameralist system; Justi's taxation rules aimed at fair burdens by ability, so flat tax is inferred as not a stated principle.

character-from-environment.rationale: Cameralists believed education, Polizei and good management could shape subjects' industry and morals.

space-expansion.rationale: Anachronistic and no cameralist source suggests this.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Absolute rule was assumed, but Seckendorff and Justi demanded rulers' duties and Justi's colleges checked the ruler's virtue; adherents are split.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Justi weighed constitutions after Montesquieu but concluded modern monarchy was best for reform, not a balance of few and many.

leader-cult.rationale: Cameralists valued the ruler's moral example and duty but not mass praise; the question is a modern one.

organic-representation.rationale: Cameralism had no representation by parties; the prince's colleges administered, and it sought to reduce guild and estate privilege (Justi), so corporate representation is not a feature.

total-state.rationale: Cameralist national management covered morals, education, religion and the economy more directly than later economic liberalism, though it was not a modern totalitarian claim.

national-rebirth.rationale: Cameralists were administrative reformers rather than regeneration movements; the rhetoric of decadence and rebirth is not found in the sources.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Justi aimed for German states to rival England and France in power, but cameralism chiefly stressed internal development; split.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Cameralism replaced feudal personal ties with a salaried bureaucracy of trained officials.

bound-labor.rationale: Cameralist writers sought productive peasants and agrarian improvement, and Justi attacked guild and feudal hindrances, though serfdom still existed in their states.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The cameralist state relies on compulsion in taxes, Polizei, conscription and workhouses for common welfare.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Anachronistic and a post-colonial idea; cameralist import substitution aimed at economic self-sufficiency, but they did not frame it this way.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Cameralism assumed a harmonious state run by officials for the common welfare; the statement concerns socialism, which it never addressed, so this is inferred from its order-and-unity premise.

land-redistribution.rationale: Cameralists wanted the state to improve agriculture and its domains, not to break up estates; inferred from their emphasis on revenue and the existing order.

refugee-return.rationale: Cameralists sought to maximise population by attracting settlers, but never addressed a right of return; inferred as indifferent.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Territorial claims in cameralist states were dynastic and fiscal rather than national; inferred from the dynastic territorial state it served.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Cameralist Polizei regulated religion and morals, but the late Enlightened writers favoured toleration; inferred at low confidence from this split.

women-must-cover.rationale: Polizei included sumptuary and morals regulation, but compulsory religious covering is not documented; inferred as unlikely.

common-currency.rationale: Coinage was a ruler's regalia and cameralists watched the balance of trade, so a shared currency would cede state control; inferred.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Cameralism served the dynastic territorial state, not pan-ethnic unity; inferred.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Cameralist administration aimed at a uniform, centrally managed territory; inferred, since the topic was not addressed.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Cameralists wanted subjects kept and productive in the territory but never addressed minority strategy; inferred as indifferent.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Cameralism held that wise legislation and trained administration shape economic life, giving ideas and policy a driving role; inferred.

ban-cartels.rationale: Cameralists curbed some guild privileges yet granted state monopolies and manufactories; adherents were split, so neutral.

no-bailouts.rationale: The cameralist state sponsored and subsidised manufactories and enterprises it judged useful; inferred that it would rescue key firms.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Authority lay with the monarch and his officials, not a majority, so the question is anachronistic; inferred opposition to majority-constraining versus bureaucratic rule is not documented, answered mildly.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Offices were held by men in this period and quotas are anachronistic; inferred.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Import substitution and a favourable trade balance are described as core cameralist economic policy, supporting a self-sufficient bloc.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Binding trade standards are anachronistic; cameralists protected the home economy by tariffs, so inferred opposition to supranational conditions.

moral-incentives.rationale: Cameralists used premiums, privileges and regulated labour to drive production, not moral appeals; inferred.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Cameralism rested on loyalty to the monarch and administrative order; inferred strong opposition to insurgent revolution.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: A strong hereditary monarch and a ranked society are the premise of the cameralist state, so abolishing hereditary privilege contradicts its core.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Cameralist texts concern administration and finance; they did not teach a civilization-centred history, so this is neutral.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Inferred from the Polizei state's paternalist duty to improve subjects' welfare, extended to dependent peoples; not addressed directly.

patriotic-education.rationale: Inferred from Polizei's concern with training loyal, useful subjects of the prince, though modern patriotic symbols are anachronistic.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Anachronistic; cameralism did not address racial preferences.

public-money-creation.rationale: Coinage was a crown regalia and the state managed the money supply for revenue, so public control of money fits; modern central banking is anachronistic.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Anachronistic; cameralists predate theories of capitalist crisis.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Not addressed; the cameralists wrote for territorial states rather than empires.

delink-world-market.rationale: Cameralists favoured import substitution and a favourable trade balance, which is mercantilist rather than delinking; inferred as mildly against.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Polizei regulation of guilds, trades and subjects' conduct left little room for unrestricted private refusal; inferred.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: A strong monarch governed through trained officials with no constitutional limits; inferred from the form of state the cameralists served.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Treaties between sovereigns were binding instruments of the territorial state; inferred from the cameralist focus on the prince's state and its territory.

elective-rulers.rationale: Cameralism sets trained officials under a strong hereditary monarch whose duty is subjects' welfare; election of rulers is not part of it.

minority-veto.rationale: The ruler and his officials decide for the state; a consent veto for dissenters is inferred to be foreign to cameralist administration.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Justi held the ruler bound by fundamental laws and welfare duties, but the cameralists did not endorse subjects' right of resistance; inferred from their support for strong monarchy.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Cameralism is a science of ruling for the monarch through his officials; a supreme parliament is the opposite of its design.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal suffering was not a cameralist subject; inferred only from their welfare concern for human subjects, so adherents give no clear answer.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Livestock, farming and use of animals were treated as economic resources for the state's output; humane limits were not discussed, so inferred.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: The ruler and state owe protection and welfare to subjects, including the poor; inferred from the paternal Polizei duties, not from a duty of the wealthy as such.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Cameralists wanted educated subjects serving the state and its welfare; inferred that private withdrawal was not their ideal.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: The cameralists favoured shaping subjects by education, censorship and Polizei, but would not describe it as pacification of the people; inferred as a rejected framing.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Cameralist rule rested on legal authority, regulation and Polizei backed by the monarch rather than on cultural hegemony; inferred.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist trade-balance thinking sees trade as moving wealth between states, but cameralists blamed poor policy, not a world structure; adherents give no clear answer.

native-born-offices.rationale: Cameralist states recruited trained officials and experts from outside, Justi himself among them; reserving offices for natives is inferred to be unneeded.

party-own-road.rationale: Communist parties are anachronistic for the 18th century; the ideology is indifferent.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Cameralism favoured import substitution and a state-directed economy aimed at self-sufficiency, so inferred support for own resources over foreign aid or investment.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Territorial growth and population counted as sources of the prince's strength; inferred support for reclaiming lost land.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Cameralist authority came from the monarch and his officials, not from descent from pre-colonial peoples; inferred from its monarchist state theory.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Anti-fascism is anachronistic for an 18th-century doctrine; no stance can be drawn from its sources.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Fascism and communism postdate cameralism; no stance can be drawn from its sources.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: The American Civil War is outside cameralism's period and concerns; no stance can be drawn.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: The cameralist state values historical order and the prince's continuity; inferred sympathy for preserving monuments, though the issue never arose.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Gender-specific disadvantage programmes are anachronistic; the Polizei welfare idea applies to all subjects but gives no clear answer.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Domestic violence services are anachronistic; Polizei regulated household order but gives no stated answer.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Cameralists tailored administration to each territory's circumstances, so inferred that institutions should fit local conditions.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The cameralist army was under the monarch and his officials; an independent political guardian role is inferred to be rejected.

paid-care-work.rationale: Cameralism never considered unpaid household work as labour; its labour policy concerned productive population, guilds and workhouses, so inferred rejection.

filial-duty.rationale: Cameralist Polizei treated the household and its moral order as a basis of the state; support for family duties is inferred from that.

office-by-exam.rationale: Cameralism's defining feature was a university-trained bureaucracy of officials with a specialised education in finance, economy and Polizei. The sources do not state this position outright; it follows from the tradition's core commitments.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: The cameralist favourable trade balance and import substitution imply state protection of domestic production; modern takeovers are anachronistic, so inferred.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Cameralist states regulated morals, marriage and religion as part of Polizei; inferred opposition to easy divorce.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Cameralism served an absolute monarch and entrusted rule to trained officials, with no place for mandated or recallable representatives.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Cameralist welfare was a state duty under Polizei, so private individual accounts are unlikely to appeal; anachronistic, inferred.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Justi respected private property and cameralists backed agrarian improvement under existing landholding, so use-based communal tenure is inferred to be rejected.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Cameralism served the prince's finances under absolutism; the ruler and his officials, not an assembly, controlled revenue and spending.

single-official-language.rationale: Cameralists in multi-ethnic Habsburg lands pursued administrative uniformity, but the sources do not settle a language policy; inferred split.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: The topic is not addressed in the sources and an inference either way is weak.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Anachronistic; the concept conflicts with a society of hierarchical estates and state-defined subjects' duties, so inferred rejection.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Cameralists favoured luxury production for trade balance, though sumptuary regulation was also part of Polizei; split.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Not addressed by cameralist writers; state interest and dynastic power politics could favour or oppose it.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Anachronistic; cameralism served dynastic power-building, but the sources do not address intervention in allied states.

corporate-influence.rationale: Inferred from its view that the trained state, not private interests, steers economic life for the common good.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred from its mercantilist control of trade and of the state's revenue and population.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Raising population was a central cameralist goal because people produced revenue and output for the state.

residents-only-property.rationale: Not addressed; the regulated estate and guild order cuts both ways.

job-guarantee.rationale: Inferred from its Polizei aim of promoting subjects' welfare, including employment and poor relief by the state.

democratic-peace.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from its monarchical rule and state-first view of foreign policy.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: It places a strong monarch and trained officials over subjects, who owe obedience.

non-intervention.rationale: Not addressed; inferred sources give no line on intervening in other states.

industrial-unions.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from its guild-era regulated economy and state direction of labour.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Inferred from its emphasis on state welfare of all subjects; the doctrine has no minority-conspiracy element.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Inferred from its Polizei regulation of marriage and population as matters of state interest.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Inferred from its rule by monarch and trained officials, where administration was not open to public scrutiny.

local-production.rationale: It favoured national self-sufficiency and import substitution, which is not the same as local production.

informal-organisation.rationale: It rests on a bureaucracy and the monarch's state, not informal groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Inferred from its territorial-state sovereignty under the monarch.

religious-nation.rationale: Not addressed; the confessional territorial state and Enlightenment-era tolerance both appear in the period.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Cameralism concerned the internal administration of a single territorial state and said little on tribute relations between states; no position is inferred.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Cameralist finance treated the territory's revenue as the prince's to direct through one central treasury, so regional retention is inferred as contrary to that centralised fiscal management.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Cameralists defended subjects' private property while the prince's domains and monopolies were state-run; the common-ownership half of the claim is not cameralist, so this is split.

defeat-communism.rationale: Communism post-dates cameralism, so the statement is anachronistic and no position is inferred.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Cameralist administration used state-run enterprises alongside chartered private manufactories and privileges, so mixed delivery under state direction is inferred.

religion-illusion.rationale: Cameralist Polizei treated religion as a support of order and morality that the state should foster, so the claim that it is a mere illusion is inferred as contrary.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Capitalism came after cameralism, whose own aim was building up state productive power; judging capitalism's progressiveness is anachronistic and adherents have no settled view.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Cameralist writers did not link women's status to the economic system and saw the household and its gender roles as natural; inferred from their view of the household as a unit of the state economy.

socialized-care.rationale: Cameralist Polizei regulated care, health and the household for the state's welfare and population, but a public-services model of housework is not addressed, so this is split.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Cameralist writers mostly wrote in German or Latin and some, like Justi, defended clear German prose, but no purge policy is documented, so this is neutral.

treaties-binding.rationale: Cameralism concerned absolutist territorial states with no doctrine on treaties with internal nations; its priority on the prince's authority and the state's interest points both ways.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Cameralists wanted a strong central bureaucracy managing the whole territory, so small self-governing property-holding communities are inferred as contrary.

majority-settlement.rationale: Cameralists sought to increase population and settled colonists in under-populated lands (peuplierung), but settling a majority group in minority regions is a different aim, so no firm position is inferred.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Cameralism predates both systems; as a state-directed mercantile economy with private property it fits neither, but it did not call for a 'third way', so the inference is weak.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Territorial claims rested on dynastic and legal title and on the state's population and revenue, not on a people's historical tie to land; inferred from the cameralist focus on administration.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from an Enlightenment-era administrative science that relied on documented records and the ruler's duty to subjects' welfare.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Sodomy was a criminal offence in the 18th-century German states whose Polizei the cameralists wrote about; inferred from their support for state regulation of morals.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Cameralist absolutism put order under the ruler and the police, and the textbooks set limits on press and associations.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The Polizei state supervised religion and allowed only limited toleration of religious parties.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Inferred from the cameralist and mercantilist aim of a favourable trade balance and import substitution; German states held few overseas colonies.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Never addressed; a question about Islamic law and jihad falls outside a Christian-era German state science, so no position is inferred.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Cameralists defended the monarch's authority as entrusted for subjects' welfare, with no religious-law test of legitimacy; inferred from that.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Cameralism put government in the hands of trained officials under a strong monarch, not in direct popular decision-making.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from a society of estates and guild regulation where the state managed groups by rank, not as overlapping oppressions.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the Polizei regulation of morals and family in a Christian state.

assisted-dying.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the state's aim of preserving and increasing the population and from Christian norms of the period.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Anachronistic; cameralism predates the left-right divide and is silent on it.

alienated-labor.rationale: Cameralists prized productive labour and ran workhouses to put people to work; they would not see it as alienating. Inferred from that.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Never addressed; inferred only that a Christian-era state science took no stance on Islam.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Seckendorff's Christian princely state and Justi's idea of authority entrusted to the ruler point to a divine or entrusted source, though Justi also used contract language; inferred.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: State churches and confessional Polizei were normal for cameralists, who did not bar religious dress; inferred from that.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Anachronistic; no basis in the sources for a position on contract law or arbitration.

social-market-economy.rationale: Cameralism favoured a state-directed economy with regulation, trade controls and state enterprises, more than a social market economy of rules and competition; inferred.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Cameralists backed standing armies and conscription as tools of state power and revenue.

rich-first.rationale: Cameralist policy aimed to raise the whole population's productivity under state direction rather than let some grow rich first; inferred.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Absolutist princes allied by dynastic interest and the sources do not discuss blocs; inferred as split.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Cameralism served hereditary territorial monarchs and took dynastic rule for granted as the frame for the trained bureaucracy.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Inferred: cameralists wanted state-directed finance and crown revenue, not user-owned mutual banks, which the tradition never discussed.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from cameralist import substitution and the ruler's sovereign control of the economy against outside constraint.

property-franchise.rationale: Cameralists did not discuss voting; subjects were ruled by officials under a monarch, and property was respected but not tied to a franchise.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Inferred: cameralism treated nature as a resource to be exploited for state wealth and had no concept of linking it to women's domination.

reification.rationale: Inferred: a pre-capitalist state science with no critique of capitalism; its writers saw economic forces as steerable by the state.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Inferred: cameralists favoured police control of the press and did not consider wealth a threat to free expression.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Cameralists valued orderly administration and codified Polizei ordinances, but upheld the ruler's discretionary decree power under absolutism.

racial-franchise.rationale: Cameralism had no racial franchise doctrine; its concern was population and subjects' welfare, and it did not set racial limits on office.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the cameralist view that policy is made by trained officials, not by citizen deliberation.

open-government-data.rationale: Inferred: absolutist cameral administration kept state finances and records as ruler's business, with no public-accountability norm.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Cameralist writers allowed limited toleration of religious parties while states of the era often restricted mixed marriage; the tradition did not settle the matter.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Inferred: cameralists wanted commerce and population to grow under state direction and did not endorse private boycotts of subjects.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Cameralism put government in the hands of trained officials serving a monarch; lot-chosen citizen bodies deciding public questions are inferred to be foreign to it.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Cameralist states supervised churches as part of Polizei but did not address reinterpreting doctrine; inferred from state-church practice, so neutral.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Cameralists sought prosperity for the monarch and his subjects, not liberty in the modern sense; inferred from their state-directed economics, which neither targets nor defends large private fortunes.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the Polizei state's regulation of morals and its 18th-century legal setting, in which same-sex acts were criminal.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Inferred from the cameralist ideal of a Christian, paternal prince whose Polizei supported religion and order; promoting unbelief is alien to it.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Inferred from the cameralist state's duty to maintain order and security through Polizei administration; abolishing coercive order would contradict it.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Inferred from cameralism's unitary state under a strong monarch and trained bureaucracy, which leaves no room for guaranteed shares of executive power.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Poor relief, workhouses and welfare were duties of the Polizei state, so cameralists would not leave the poor mainly to private charity; inferred from that duty.

term-limits.rationale: Inferred from rule by a hereditary monarch served by career officials trained in the cameral sciences; elected office was not part of the system.

vote-delegation.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from a system in which subjects had no vote and the monarch and his officials decided policy.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: The tradition never addressed it; its concern with population and state wealth gives no clear answer on civilisational catastrophe.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Inferred from 18th-century German state churches, which reserved clerical and teaching offices to men.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred from the Hausvater household model of the period, where the husband headed the household; the cameralists did not question it.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Cameralist government was monarchical and bureaucratic with no popular local votes; Justi welcomed immigrants as population but not as voters. Inferred.

rent-control.rationale: Cameralist Polizei regulated prices and economic life in the interest of welfare; rent caps are an inference from that tradition.

abolish-ip.rationale: Cameralists granted privileges to manufactures and Justi respected private property; abolishing patents and copyrights is inferred to be contrary to this.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Cameralists backed conscription and the education of subjects for the state, but drilled youth movements are anachronistic; inferred.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Anachronistic; nothing in cameralism bears on nuclear weapons.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Cameralism aimed at a strong, self-sufficient territorial state under its own monarch, so foreign garrisons would run against it; inferred, and subsidy treaties show practice varied.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Anachronistic; cameralists did not address recognition of past mass killings.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Cameralists held that those who do not work should not eat and favoured workhouses, but Justi respected private property; inferred that useful labour was prized above idle ownership.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Cameralist writers supported conscription, war and the death penalty as state powers; absolute non-violence is inferred to be foreign to them.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Cameralism concerned dynastic territorial states, not national identity from ancient origins; no position is stated.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Anachronistic; the sources have no equivalent concept.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Anachronistic; feminist theory lies outside cameralism.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Cameralism served the dynastic state and its welfare aims and did not develop a cult of national martyrs; inferred.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Cameralism treated government as a secular science of administration and welfare, with only limited toleration of religious parties; inferred that it did not see politics as a struggle of good and evil.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Anachronistic; cameralists concerned territorial subjects, not diasporas.

culture-before-state.rationale: The cameralist programme was the building and administration of the state, with officials trained to manage it; cultural renewal first is contrary to this by inference.

god-not-male.rationale: Anachronistic; not addressed in the sources.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Anachronistic; not addressed in the sources.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Cameralists valued any productive subject or immigrant for population and revenue and wanted trade for state wealth, so ethnic reservation of the economy is not their aim; inferred.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Cameralism consolidated dynastic territories, not units for one people; no position in the sources.

independent-unions.rationale: Unions did not exist, but cameralists put guilds and trades under state regulation and Justi reduced guild power, so autonomous bodies were not favoured.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Cameralism placed power in the monarch and his trained officials, not the working class; inferred from that structure.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Polizei made provision of public welfare, health and works a state duty, so basic services under public authority fit; modern ownership questions are inferred.

second-chamber.rationale: Cameralists favoured a strong monarch with a trained bureaucracy rather than representative checks; inferred from their absolutist stance.

municipal-property.rationale: Cameralism favoured state-directed economic life while respecting private property, with no place for community ownership; inferred.

confederal-coordination.rationale: The cameralist state centralised administration under the prince, so local assemblies holding all decisions runs against it; inferred.

family-wage.rationale: Cameralists regulated wages and prices and cared for the population, but a family wage was never put forward as a principle.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Polizei regulated physicians and medicines for public health, but speed against caution was not discussed, so this is split.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Inferred from the cameralist aim of increasing population and productive subjects through state action, which favours funding life-extending research.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Inferred from the cameralist focus on state revenue and tax collection, which depends on the state tracing and controlling money flows.

online-anonymity.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from cameralist Polizei controls on press, speech and conduct, which favour officials knowing who acts.

person-over-state.rationale: Justi and Jung-Stilling held that the state's purpose is subjects' welfare and spoke of rights of humanity, yet the ruler's wealth and power remained the aim; adherents were split.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Cameralist Polizei covered religion and morals as state concerns, so politics was meant to serve more than material welfare; inferred.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: In the territorial state the prince's authority was supreme over estates and localities, so lower powers were held at the ruler's pleasure; inferred.

gm-crops.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from cameralism's drive to raise agricultural and productive output by state-promoted improvement.

dense-cities.rationale: Cameralists promoted manufacture and population but gave no environmental view of cities, so this is neutral.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Cameralism concerned the territorial state and all its subjects as a resource; racial organisation was not part of it. Inferred.

racial-pride.rationale: The concept of racial pride does not appear in cameralist writing, which attached loyalty to the prince and state.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Cameralists aimed to build state revenue and conscripted force for the prince's power, and did not limit it to defence; inferred.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Cameralism served the territorial state and its subjects rather than a linguistic nation, so it never took a position; inferred at low confidence.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred: cameralist writers favoured one body of subjects under a single sovereign administered by state officials, not self-governing religious communities.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Mercantilist rivalry between states was assumed, but the sources describe no partition-plot theme.

free-public-college.rationale: Inferred: cameralism had states fund university chairs to train officials, but free tuition for all is anachronistic.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Anachronistic; cameralists managed resources such as forests for state revenue but did not propose pollution taxes.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred from cameralist concern for the lasting productivity of the state's land, forests and population; the sources do not state it as a duty to future generations.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Not addressed by the cameralist sources; inferred neutral.

arms-reduction.rationale: Inferred: cameralists valued a strong army as a source of the monarch's power and revenue, so limiting arms was not a goal.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Inferred: cameralism assumed absolutist monarchs conducting state affairs by officials, with secret treaties usual in the period.

capital-controls.rationale: Cameralism sought a favourable trade balance and import substitution through state direction of economic life, which implies controlling the flow of money abroad.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Inferred: cameralist writers wanted standing armies under the prince's authority and regulated by Polizei, though private arms were not discussed as a modern question.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Inferred: cameralism served a strong monarch whose officials supplied revenue and conscripts for state needs, so conscientious refusal of state wars is contrary to its principles.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Inferred: cameralist Polizei regulated guilds, wages and trades from above, so wages set by group bargaining between unions and employers is anachronistic and cuts across state regulation.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Cameralists wanted the state to promote subjects' welfare and employment, but income top-ups through tax credits are anachronistic and not documented.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Inferred: cameralism made the prince's officials masters of public finance and revenue, so legal limits on the sovereign's borrowing sit badly with it, though cameralists also prized sound budgets.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Inferred: cameralists pursued a favourable trade balance and import substitution for their own state, not reform of international rules for poorer countries.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Cameralism is the science of building and running the bureaucratic state under a strong monarch, so destroying that machinery is the opposite of its aims.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Inferred: cameralists wanted the state to direct economic life through trained officials, not let communities choose their own systems.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Inferred: cameralists treated forests, mines and land as sources of state revenue to be managed and accounted for, though not as modern natural capital.

sacred-nation.rationale: Cameralism was loyal to the prince and territorial state, not to a sacred nation, which is a later notion.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Student loans did not exist, and cameralists favoured training officials at state expense but never discussed debt relief.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Inferred: cameralism treated the territory as a single economic unit to be developed for the whole state's welfare, not as a core exploiting a periphery.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Jung-Stilling's textbook speaks of rights of humanity and welfare as the state's purpose, which fits a shared human nature, though redesigning human nature is not discussed.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred: cameralist Polizei supervised the press and censored publications, so media independent of government control contradicts it.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Cameralist rulers regulated and supervised churches, and Jung-Stilling allows only limited toleration of religious parties, implying an established truth over relativism; inferred, as the claim is not addressed directly.

farm-price-support.rationale: Cameralists directed agriculture and food supply as part of Polizei to raise population and revenue, and Justi promoted state economic management; guaranteed prices are inferred, not stated.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Nuclear weapons are anachronistic; inferred from cameralism's concern with the ruler's military strength and security of the state.

workers-own-party.rationale: Cameralism is monarchical administration by trained officials for the ruler's welfare aims, so independent class parties are anachronistic and alien to it; inferred.

ban-fgm.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the cameralist view that the state's Polizei protects subjects' welfare and bodily safety, though customary practice was not an explicit target.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Cameralists regulated property and inheritance under Polizei and civil law, but the sources do not give a position on equal inheritance for women; adherents split.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Language naming was not a cameralist question, and the sources give no position.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Cameralist Polizei was ex ante state regulation of economic life and public welfare, the opposite of leaving harms to private suits; inferred.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Cameralism put authority in the monarch and trained officials, not in estates or customary bodies; inferred from its bureaucratic absolutism, as chiefs are not discussed.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Polizei gave the state wide power to limit subjects' liberty for welfare, and cameralists regulated forests and mines for the common good; inferred, as environmentalism is anachronistic.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Cameralist absolutism favoured strong state control and the ruler's fixed police and penal ordinances over discretion; inferred, as sentencing is not directly discussed.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Cameralists sought a unified, productive population under the state and Polizei regulated subjects' conduct; a language requirement is inferred, not stated.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Cameralist Polizei regulated trades through guilds and the state ordered economic life; a ban on compulsory association is anachronistic and inferred from this regulating stance.

voter-id.rationale: Cameralism had no elections or voting; the question is anachronistic and the answer is split.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Cameralist writers such as Jung-Stilling allowed only limited toleration of religious parties under state supervision; inferred as favouring an established religion over equal precedence.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Justi and the cameralists defended monarchical absolutism justified by the ruler's duty to subjects' welfare, not election; inferred as rejecting a procedural test of legitimacy.

premarital-sex.rationale: Polizei ordinances policed morals and public order, and the sources show religion and morals as state concerns; inferred, since the topic is not stated.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Cameralist Polizei limited the press and policed public order as a state duty; extending this to modern communications is an inference.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Cameralism favoured paternalist poor relief, workhouses and state management of the poor rather than unconditional cash; inferred from Jung-Stilling's workhouse policy.

women-suffrage.rationale: Political rights were held by estates and the monarch, and cameralist texts do not extend them to women; inferred from the absolutist, hierarchical order.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Cameralists treated religion as an ally of order and morals; the claim is anachronistic and is inferred as rejected.

race-social-construct.rationale: Race as a concept is not treated in the cameralist sources; neither answer can be derived from its principles.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Cameralists favoured state agencies for welfare and population, but gender equality was not an aim and hierarchy of status was assumed; inferred.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Inferred: cameralists had the state regulate land and resources, including crown domains, so first-come ownership is not their principle; the sources do not discuss it directly.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the cameralist emphasis on the monarch's sovereignty over his territory, which sits poorly with courts above the state.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Cameralists were Lutheran or Catholic officials, but their science of administration took no position on scriptural literalism.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the hierarchical, paternal monarchical order the cameralists assumed, which had no such requirement.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the cameralist commitment to state-directed economic life run by trained officials, which they would want preserved, though they did not know modern planning.

indirect-election.rationale: Inferred: cameralism assumed appointed officials under a strong monarch, so filling offices by delegates from councils is foreign to it.

national-church-status.rationale: Inferred: cameralist states generally had an established state church whose clergy served as part of the administration of subjects' welfare.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from its centralising aim of a uniform bureaucratic administration of the whole territory under the monarch.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from its dynastic view that territory belongs to the monarch's state and is settled by rulers, not popular votes.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Cameralism predates decolonisation and had no view; its concern was increasing the state's population and revenue, not border stability.

simple-living.rationale: Inferred: cameralists sought growth of population, manufacture and trade to raise state revenue and welfare, which cuts against limiting needs.
